provenance.review: machine-checked by lab.tools.check_registry (verbatim quotes, sections, ids); content reviewed by Claude where noted in review_notes

draft_notes: Only the supplied text was used. Requirement identifiers preserve the carriage return in the supplied prefix as JSON \r. Repeated rules are consolidated: §9.2 repeats §3.11; §9.5 reinforces §3.3; the oracle-inconsistency rule in §12 repeats §3.3.2; invariants 1, 2, 4, 5 and 7 in §13 repeat §§1, 4, 6 and 7. Separate entries capture the additional §13 prohibitions and requirements. The front matter lists DKP-0-ORACLE-001, DKP-1-IMPACT-001 and DKP-1-IDENTITY-001 as document-wide dependencies without assigning them to specific provisions; their contents were not supplied. §2 states a system-position sequence but no independently testable obligation. §4 requires positive SPDₖ when its antecedent holds, whereas §§3.6 and 5 permit zero; no precedence rule resolves this conflict. Informational SPDₖ is not defined as a numeric value, and its treatment in aggregation is unspecified. The aggregation domain for Σ Aₖ is also unspecified.

requirements.title: Protocol override is prohibited
requirements.interpretation: A checker could reject operations classified as overrides of this protocol. The text does not define an override or distinguish it operationally from the controlled changes permitted by §15.
requirements.criterion: No operation classified as an override is permitted.
requirements.gap: An override is a declared attempt by another protocol; changes through UPGRADE are checked under the finality clause.
hypotheses_needed: Define how overrides differ from amendments under §15.

requirements.title: Recognition requires measured risk suppression
requirements.quote: Preventive contribution is recognized only through measurable suppression of activated risk processes, not through absence of realized harm and not through hypothetical projections.
requirements.interpretation: Recognition records must cite measured suppression of an activated risk process. Absence of harm or hypothetical projections cannot supply the recognition basis; deciding whether evidence measures actual suppression requires an evidence model.
requirements.criterion: Every recognized preventive contribution is supported by measured suppression of activated risk, rather than absence of harm or hypothetical projections.
requirements.gap: Activation and suppression are the bench's measured TA and SE; their thresholds are L8 (§14).
hypotheses_needed: Declare an evidence model for activated risk and measured suppression.

requirements.title: Protected zones have physical boundaries
requirements.interpretation: A protected-zone record must identify a physically bounded evaluation domain. Testing that condition requires a representation connecting the recorded boundary to physical space.
requirements.criterion: Z is a physically bounded domain used for evaluation.
requirements.gap: The representation and validation of physical boundaries are unspecified. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare a spatial representation and a method for validating physical boundaries.

requirements.title: Risk channels derive from PTL
requirements.interpretation: Risk-channel records must carry PTL provenance and represent measurable risk exposure. PTL and the measurement requirements are not defined in this document.
requirements.criterion: Each Rcᵢ is PTL-derived and represents measurable risk exposure.
requirements.gap: PTL provenance validation and measurable risk exposure are not operationally specified. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare valid PTL provenance and an exposure measurement model.

requirements.title: Activation requires independent oracle classes
requirements.quote: TAₖ valid ⇔ confirmations ≥ 2 independent oracle classes
requirements.interpretation: Given confirmation records and an explicit independence relation between oracle classes, validity must equal the result of the class-count test. Two confirmations from a single class do not satisfy the stated condition.
requirements.criterion: TAₖ is valid if and only if confirmations come from at least 2 independent oracle classes.
data_dependencies: oracle class identities and independence attestations

requirements.title: Compute oracle intensity spread
requirements.interpretation: Compute the maximum minus the minimum over the relevant intensity set. The text does not specify whether this set includes all oracle readings or only valid readings, and it gives no empty-set behavior.
requirements.criterion: Δ_oracle equals max(intensity) − min(intensity) over the applicable oracle intensity set.
requirements.gap: The included oracle population and behavior for an empty intensity set are unspecified. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare which readings enter the spread calculation and how an empty set is handled.

requirements.title: Consistent activation uses minimum intensity
requirements.interpretation: When Δ_oracle ≤ ε_consistency, the activation intensity must equal the minimum valid oracle intensity. The consistency threshold comes from §14, and valid-reading selection must be supplied.
requirements.criterion: If Δ_oracle ≤ ε_consistency, TAₖ_intensity equals min(valid oracle intensities).
requirements.gap: The calibrated threshold and the rule selecting valid oracle intensities are not supplied. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the valid-reading selection rule and behavior when no valid intensity exists.

requirements.title: Inconsistent signals become informational
requirements.interpretation: When Δ_oracle > ε_consistency, the event contribution must receive informational status. This rule is repeated in §12; the document does not specify the encoding or downstream arithmetic treatment of that status.
requirements.criterion: If Δ_oracle > ε_consistency, SPDₖ is informational.
hypotheses_needed: Declare how informational SPDₖ is represented.

requirements.title: Interventions are measured and windowed
requirements.quote: Measured Subject action within valid space-time window.
requirements.interpretation: An SIₖ must identify a measured action by a Subject within a valid spatial and temporal window. The text does not establish whether this window is the same as the TAₖ-to-SEₖ alignment window in §3.6.
requirements.criterion: SIₖ represents a measured Subject action occurring within the valid space-time window.
requirements.gap: The valid space-time window and action-measurement acceptance rules are undefined. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the intervention window and whether its temporal component uses Δt_int.
Declare what evidence establishes a measured Subject action.

requirements.title: Suppression events concern active risk
requirements.interpretation: An SEₖ must be supported by measurement of a reduction or interruption of risk that was active. A checker needs a model relating the measurements to active risk and suppression.
requirements.criterion: SEₖ represents measured reduction or interruption of active risk.
requirements.gap: The measurement model establishing active risk and reduction or interruption is unspecified. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare how measurements establish active risk and its reduction or interruption.

requirements.title: Suppression follows activation within window
requirements.quote:
TAₖ @ t₀
SEₖ @ t₁, where 0 < (t₁ − t₀) ≤ Δt_int
requirements.interpretation: Compare matched activation and suppression timestamps. Suppression must occur strictly after activation and no later than the calibrated interval limit.
requirements.criterion: 0 < t₁ − t₀ ≤ Δt_int.
hypotheses_needed: Declare a common time basis for the matched signals.

requirements.title: Compute clamped suppression completeness
requirements.interpretation: Calculate the stated relative reduction and clamp it between 0 and 1. The quotient is undefined for zero activation intensity unless the separate zero-completeness branch applies, and branch precedence is not explicit.
requirements.criterion: Where the quotient is defined, Sₖ equals clamp(0,1,(TAₖ_intensity − SEₖ_intensity)/TAₖ_intensity).
hypotheses_needed: Declare zero-denominator handling and the precedence of the conditional Sₖ = 0 rule.

requirements.title: Nondecreasing intensity gives zero contribution
requirements.interpretation: If suppression-event intensity is at least activation intensity, both completeness and contribution must be zero. This is directly checkable, although §4 can simultaneously demand a positive contribution.
requirements.criterion: SEₖ_intensity ≥ TAₖ_intensity implies Sₖ = 0 and SPDₖ = 0.

requirements.title: Severity weights are nonnegative scalars
requirements.interpretation: Check that each supplied severity weight is a scalar with a value at least zero. Its actual calibrated value is governed separately by §14.
requirements.criterion: Wₖ is a scalar and Wₖ ≥ 0.

requirements.title: Attribution factors remain within bounds
requirements.interpretation: Check each attribution factor against the inclusive interval from 0 to 1.

requirements.title: Confidence derives from PTL coverage
requirements.interpretation: Confidence must be derived from PTL coverage, so provenance can be checked against coverage inputs. The document provides no function that determines the resulting confidence value.
requirements.criterion: Cₖ is derived from PTL coverage.
requirements.gap: The mapping from PTL coverage to Cₖ is missing. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare a coverage-to-confidence function.

requirements.title: Tamper factors derive from detection
requirements.interpretation: The tamper-resistance factor must depend on manipulation-detection results. Apart from later directional and zeroing rules, no mapping is specified.
requirements.criterion: Tₖ is derived from manipulation detection.
requirements.gap: The mapping from manipulation detection to Tₖ is missing. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare a manipulation-detection model and its mapping to Tₖ.

requirements.title: Contextual baselines serve audit only
requirements.interpretation: CBFᵢ may serve as an audit reference and must not produce reward. §9.2 repeats the non-reward requirement; whether any indirect influence on reward is forbidden is not specified.
requirements.criterion: CBFᵢ is used only as an audit reference and is non-reward.
hypotheses_needed: Declare whether non-reward prohibits indirect as well as direct reward influence.

requirements.title: Recognition requires the signal conjunction
requirements.interpretation: For supplied validity, consistency and event predicates, the conjunction requires positive SPDₖ; otherwise SPDₖ must be zero or informational. The positive branch conflicts with zero factors allowed elsewhere, and the text does not choose between zero and informational in the general fallback.
requirements.criterion: If TAₖ is valid and consistent and SIₖ and SEₖ exist, SPDₖ > 0; otherwise SPDₖ = 0 or SPDₖ is informational.

requirements.title: Multiply preventive contribution factors
requirements.quote: SPDₖ = Wₖ × Sₖ × Aₖ × Cₖ × Tₖ
requirements.interpretation: For numeric contribution records, compare SPDₖ with the product of the five supplied factors. This arithmetic check does not resolve how informational records interact with the formula.
requirements.criterion: For numeric SPDₖ, SPDₖ = Wₖ × Sₖ × Aₖ × Cₖ × Tₖ.

requirements.title: Aggregate contributions for each subject
requirements.interpretation: Compare a subject's score with the sum of that subject's applicable event contributions. The event inclusion period, duplicate handling and treatment of informational records are unspecified.
requirements.criterion: PS_subject equals Σ SPDₖ over the applicable contributions for the subject.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the aggregation period, event inclusion and duplicate rules, and treatment of informational SPDₖ.

requirements.title: Positive attribution requires traceable causality
requirements.interpretation: Positive attribution and traceable causal linkage must imply each other. A checker can apply the equivalence after a declared evidence model determines whether causal linkage is traceable.
requirements.criterion: Aₖ > 0 if and only if causal linkage is traceable.
requirements.gap: Checks the bench's formalization (A > 0 only for recognized interventions); causal linkage itself is a scenario input, not inferred from measurements.
hypotheses_needed: Declare a causal attribution model and evidence requirements for traceability.

requirements.title: Cap attribution and preserve residual
requirements.interpretation: Within the applicable attribution pool, factors must sum to at most 1 and any residual must remain unallocated. The text does not state whether the pool spans subjects for one event, events for one subject, or another grouping.
requirements.criterion: Σ Aₖ ≤ 1 within the applicable pool, and the residual remains unallocated.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the attribution pool over which the cap and residual rule apply.

requirements.title: Attribution cannot create justice consequences
requirements.interpretation: Check that preventive attribution creates none of the listed consequences: obligation, liability or duty presumption. This requires a model that identifies those consequences and traces their creation to attribution.
requirements.criterion: Preventive attribution creates no obligation, liability or duty presumption.
requirements.gap: Observed as obligation, liability or duty fields on outputs.
hypotheses_needed: Declare a justice-state model and causal provenance rules for attribution effects.

requirements.title: Prove interventions without exposing logs
requirements.quote:
Subject-linked intervention must be provable via:

ZKP(SIₖ, linkage) without exposing raw behavioral logs
requirements.interpretation: Verify that a zero-knowledge proof can establish SIₖ and linkage without disclosing raw behavioral logs. The text does not identify the proof statement, proof system or disclosure model.
requirements.criterion: SIₖ and linkage are provable via ZKP(SIₖ, linkage) without exposure of raw behavioral logs.
requirements.gap: The bench has a ZKP placeholder only; the check reports UNKNOWN.
hypotheses_needed: Declare a proof system, its intervention-and-linkage statement, and a disclosure threat model.

requirements.title: Protect raw behavioral log access
requirements.interpretation: Raw logs must simultaneously be encrypted, access-restricted and audit-gated. Configuration and access records could support checks after the encryption, authorization and audit-gate requirements are defined.
requirements.criterion: All raw logs are encrypted, access-restricted and audit-gated.
requirements.gap: Acceptable encryption, access restrictions and audit-gate behavior are unspecified. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare encryption requirements, authorized access and the audit-gate mechanism.

requirements.title: Self-induced risk eliminates tamper factor
requirements.interpretation: If the subject-to-activation linkage score exceeds θ, Tₖ must be zero. Equality does not trigger this particular rule; linkage scoring is undefined and θ is assigned to L8.
requirements.criterion: linkage(subject, TAₖ) > θ implies Tₖ = 0.
requirements.gap: contribution: Self-induced linkage as detected by the bench. prevention: Checks T = 0 for observed linkage > θ; how linkage is measured is a scenario hypothesis (H-L).
hypotheses_needed: Declare how linkage(subject, TAₖ) is measured.

requirements.title: Recurring threat patterns reduce resistance
requirements.interpretation: A repeated activation pattern must reduce Tₖ. Testing this requires a definition of pattern recurrence and a comparison baseline; the text gives neither the reduction magnitude nor behavior at a lower bound.
requirements.criterion: When a TAₖ pattern repeats, Tₖ decreases.
requirements.gap: Pattern equivalence, recurrence window, comparison baseline and reduction rule are unspecified. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare a recurrence detector, comparison baseline and Tₖ reduction model.

requirements.title: Low coverage reduces confidence
requirements.interpretation: Low coverage must reduce Cₖ relative to an appropriate reference. The reference could be a preceding value or a higher-coverage comparison, and neither reading is selected by the text.
requirements.criterion: Low coverage causes Cₖ to decrease.
requirements.gap: The low-coverage criterion, comparison reference and confidence adjustment are unspecified. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare what counts as low coverage and the reference and rule for decreasing Cₖ.

requirements.title: Absent data forces zero contribution
requirements.interpretation: An event with no applicable data must receive zero SPDₖ. The text does not specify whether no data means no readings at all, no valid readings, or absence of any required input.
requirements.criterion: No data implies SPDₖ = 0.
hypotheses_needed: Declare which data absence triggers zero SPDₖ.

requirements.title: Peer signals cannot generate reward
requirements.interpretation: Reward provenance must exclude peer signals as a reward basis. The document does not define peer signals or clarify whether indirect reward influence is prohibited.
requirements.criterion: Peer signals are non-reward.
requirements.gap: Peer signals and the scope of non-reward influence are undefined. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare peer-signal classification and whether indirect reward influence is excluded.

requirements.title: Enforce the global floors
requirements.interpretation: A checker would verify that applicable values never violate the global floors. The document supplies neither the floors nor the quantities and scope to which they apply.
requirements.criterion: Every value governed by a global floor satisfies that floor.
requirements.gap: The governed quantities, floor values and enforcement scope are missing. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the global floors, their governed quantities and enforcement scope.

requirements.title: Output contribution and attribution fields
requirements.interpretation: Check that the protocol output includes event contribution, subject aggregate and attribution information. Field types and encoding are unspecified, but presence of these semantic fields is testable on a supplied structured output.
requirements.criterion: The output includes SPDₖ, PS_subject and attribution.

requirements.title: Output confidence and tamper flags
requirements.interpretation: Check that the protocol output includes confidence information and tamper flags. The required presence is explicit, although their detailed schemas are not supplied.
requirements.criterion: The output includes confidence and tamper flags.

requirements.title: Outputs are deterministic and auditable
requirements.interpretation: Repeated evaluation with identical complete inputs and configuration should produce identical outputs, and records should permit an audit. The document does not specify the complete input boundary or the evidence needed for auditability.
requirements.criterion: Outputs are deterministic for identical complete inputs and are auditable.
hypotheses_needed: Declare all state treated as evaluation input and the evidence required for an audit.

requirements.title: Ambiguous attribution yields zero contribution
requirements.interpretation: When attribution is classified as ambiguous, SPDₖ must be zero. The classification requires an ambiguity criterion absent from this text.
requirements.criterion: Attribution ambiguity implies SPDₖ = 0.
requirements.gap: Checks the bench reading H-A-2 (ambiguity := claims of eligible subjects sum above 1).
hypotheses_needed: Declare an attribution ambiguity criterion.

requirements.title: Sensor degradation reduces confidence
requirements.interpretation: Sensor degradation must reduce Cₖ. A checker needs a degradation assessment and a reference confidence value; no reduction magnitude or functional relationship is given.
requirements.criterion: Sensor degradation causes Cₖ to decrease.
requirements.gap: Sensor degradation, the comparison reference and the confidence reduction rule are unspecified. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare a sensor degradation model and the reference and rule for confidence reduction.

requirements.title: Hypothetical states are prohibited
requirements.interpretation: A checker could reject hypothetical states in the protocol's evidence or calculations after the applicable state domain is defined. The literal wording could prohibit all hypothetical states, while its context could limit the prohibition to attribution and reward states; §14 separately contemplates simulation.
requirements.criterion: No hypothetical states are used within the scope of this invariant.
data_dependencies: state usage in attribution and simulation
requirements.gap: Checked on the S factor (from measured TA and SE) and the factor set; the bench is the verified v2.1.1, not modified.
hypotheses_needed: Declare whether the invariant applies only to operational attribution or also to simulation states.

requirements.title: Anti-gaming enforcement remains mandatory
requirements.interpretation: The specific anti-manipulation provisions can be checked through their individual entries. This broader invariant has no defined completeness criterion for deciding whether anti-gaming is enforced beyond those provisions.
requirements.criterion: Anti-gaming is enforced.
requirements.gap: The document does not define what constitutes sufficient anti-gaming enforcement.
hypotheses_needed: Declare whether compliance with §§9–10 exhausts this invariant or whether an additional adversarial model is required.

requirements.title: Simulation layer defines operative parameters
requirements.interpretation: The simulation layer must define ε_consistency, Δt_int, θ thresholds and Wₖ weights. Their provenance can be checked, but the text provides neither the values nor a simulation procedure for deriving them.
requirements.criterion: L8 defines ε_consistency, Δt_int, θ thresholds and Wₖ weights.
requirements.gap: The simulation outputs and parameter derivation procedure are not supplied. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the simulation model used to define the listed parameters.

requirements.title: Changes follow the controlled procedure
requirements.quote: This protocol is changed only through the controlled procedure of DKP-4-UPGRADE-001: proposal, simulation under DKP-8-SIMULATION-001, audit under DKP-8-AUDIT-001, acceptance conditions, activation window and rollback.
requirements.interpretation: Normative protocol changes require the listed controlled-procedure elements and conformance to the referenced upgrade, simulation and audit documents. The presentation-only exception appears later in this section; the external procedural requirements are unavailable.
requirements.criterion: Every normative protocol change follows DKP-4-UPGRADE-001 with proposal, simulation under DKP-8-SIMULATION-001, audit under DKP-8-AUDIT-001, acceptance conditions, activation window and rollback.
requirements.gap: Declared stages of the change; the procedure itself is upgrade_lifecycle.
hypotheses_needed: If simulating without the referenced documents, explicitly declare substitute workflow, acceptance, activation and rollback rules.

requirements.title: Changes require versioning and migration
requirements.quote:
- version increment
- compatibility audit
- migration path
requirements.interpretation: For a normative change, verify a version increment, a compatibility audit and a migration path. The text does not define version ordering or standards for the audit and migration path.
requirements.criterion: A normative change includes a version increment, compatibility audit and migration path.
requirements.gap: No version ordering is defined; presence is declared. No standard for the audit; presence is declared. No standard for the migration path; presence is declared.
hypotheses_needed: Declare version ordering and acceptance criteria for compatibility audits and migration paths.

requirements.title: Presentation corrections use date recording
requirements.quote: Presentation-only corrections that do not change normative content are not Upgrades (DKP-4-UPGRADE-001 §3); they are recorded only by the "Last updated" date of this document.
requirements.interpretation: A correction classified as presentation-only and normatively unchanged is exempt from Upgrade classification and is recorded only through the document's Last updated date. Determining normative equivalence requires a classification method or review, and the referenced upgrade definition is absent.
requirements.criterion: If a correction is presentation-only and changes no normative content, it is not an Upgrade and is recorded only by the document's Last updated date.
hypotheses_needed: Declare how presentation-only changes and normative equivalence are established.
Declare whether the front-matter last_updated field implements the quoted Last updated date.
